about.title: About dayday330
about.intro:
dayday330 is a public mental health promotion initiative launched by New Life Psychiatric Rehabilitation Association in 2019. It encourages everyone to set aside time each day to practise "3-3-0 micro-breaks" — small moments to care for the Body (3), Mind (3) and Spirit (0) in ways that suit their personal preferences and lifestyle.

Research has shown that taking daily micro-breaks can effectively relieve emotional strain and reduce stress. Through simple and sustainable practices, individuals can gradually build healthier habits and strengthen their overall well-being.

We also encourage participants to draw inspiration from the "Five Ways to Wellbeing" proposed by the New Economics Foundation in the UK when choosing their 330 micro-break activities. These include: Take Notice, Be Active, Give, Connect, and Keep Learning. By incorporating these elements into everyday life, individuals can nourish their body, mind and spirit, and steadily cultivate a more fulfilling life.
about.content1:
330 Day is the annual flagship mental wellness campaign organised by dayday330 every March. Since 2019, we have continuously introduced large-scale public initiatives in different formats to promote the concept of 330 micro-breaks — encouraging people to reserve a small moment each day to care for their body, mind and spirit, and to gradually reshape their life rhythm through small but meaningful changes.

330 Day 2026 – Sense · To Live is a month-long, city-wide initiative taking place throughout March. Through experiences engaging the five senses — sight, sound, smell, taste and touch — participants are invited to rediscover the present moment within familiar daily settings and practise awareness within the urban environment.

Through a series of interactive missions and experiential activities, the programme encourages "sensing" to become part of everyday living. By cultivating sustainable micro-break habits, participants can reconnect with themselves, their communities and the rhythm of the city.
about.content:
330 Day 2026 Sense · To Live is a month-long, city-wide initiative taking place throughout March. Through experiences engaging the five senses—sight, sound, smell, taste, and touch—the programme invites participants to reconnect with the present moment within familiar daily settings. By encouraging sustainable micro-break habits, Sense · To Live integrates mindful sensing into everyday life, making "feeling" a natural part of living.

How Sense · To Live Works

The City Five Senses Journey
During the campaign period, participants can take part in five senses themed missions across different corners of the city, in collaboration with dayday330 partners and designated locations.

Each mission is designed to be short, accessible, and repeatable, allowing participants to engage consciously with their senses without disrupting their existing daily routines.

Five-Senses Missions Include (but are not limited to):

Sight
Rediscover overlooked details in everyday surroundings through observation and visual awareness.
Sound
Pause to listen and recognize layers and rhythms within the surrounding environment.
Smell
Notice how scents evoke memories and emotional responses.
Taste
Engage fully in the act of eating, paying attention to texture, flavor, and change.
Touch
Heighten bodily awareness through sensations such as temperature, weight, and texture.

After completing each mission, participants may record their experiences on the designated 330 Day mobile page, gradually building a personal collection of five-senses experiences.
Participation & Game Mechanics

Join the Journey
Participants may join the Sense · To Live via the 330 Day mobile page to access campaign guidelines and mission details.

Complete Five Senses Missions
Participants follow instructions to complete sensory missions at partner locations or within their daily lives. The missions emphasize self-awareness, with no standard answers and no right or wrong outcomes.

Collect Five Senses Stamps
Each completed mission earns a corresponding five senses stamp. By collecting a designated number of stamps, participants can unlock commemorative rewards at different stages of the journey.

Reward Redemption
During the campaign period, participants who complete the designated five-senses missions and successfully collect the required stamps may redeem 330 Day 2026 limited-edition commemorative items at *designated locations.

Designated locations include:

Redemption Notes:
Each participant is eligible to redeem one commemorative item corresponding to their achieved reward tier during the campaign period.
Quantities are limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis, while stocks last.

Closing Event – Five Senses Carnival

As one of the key highlights of 330 Day 2026 Sense · To Live, a closing event titled "Five Senses Carnival" will be held on 28–29 March 2026 at The Wai, Tai Wai, bringing together the collective five-senses experiences from throughout March through a variety of interactive booths.

The event will showcase selected five senses themed interactive content and experiential installations, allowing participants to revisit and extend their sensory journey from the past month within a shared physical space. Through participation and exchange, the public is invited to complete a collective five senses moment belonging to the city.

A Closing Ceremony will take place on 29 March 2026, marking a meaningful conclusion to the Sense ·To Live.

Five Senses Carnival

Date: 28–29 March 2026 (Saturday & Sunday)
Time: 10:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.
Venue: L2, The Wai,18 Che Kung Miu Road, Sha Tin

Programme Highlights:
The festival will feature multiple interactive booths themed around the five senses, along with 330 Micro-break activities and well-being experiences. Public are invited to connect with themselves in a relaxed and accessible way, and to experience how the five senses can bring subtle yet meaningful changes to everyday life.

wellbeing.description: Please select the option that best matches your situation
wellbeing.please_answer_all: Please answer all questions before submitting
wellbeing.disclaimer_content: The dayday330 well-being index is intended as a self-assessment tool to provide the general public with a preliminary understanding of their current mental health status. The result of the assessment is for reference only and should not be regarded as equivalent to any formal diagnosis made by healthcare professionals. Should you have any enquiries or further needs, please seek professional assessment or support.

high.title: 330 Holistic well-being
high.description:
Your current physical, psychological, and spiritual well-being is above average, reflecting good physical and mental condition with a relatively high level of positive feelings. In general, you connect well with those around you and your surroundings. You have a sound understanding of your own values, which contributes to a flourishing life.

Your dedication to taking care of your well-being is appreciated. To maintain your holistic well-being, we encourage you to engage in nurturing activities consistently on a daily basis, such as:

• Practise mindfulness
• Exercise regularly
• Connect with nature
• Savour your favourite things
• Do something you feel like doing
• Learn new things
• Connect and share with people
• Help people in need
• Participate in volunteer services

average.title: Well-being is average
average.description:
Your current physical, psychological, and spiritual well-being is at an average level, reflecting an adequate level of positive emotions. Your current activities can generally meet your social and spiritual needs.

Your effort to take care of yourself is appreciated. To further enhance your holistic well-being, we encourage you to pay more attention to and take care of your physical, mental, and spiritual needs. You may build up your self-care routine including nurturing activities of your choice on a daily basis, such as:

• Practise mindfulness
• Exercise regularly
• Connect with nature
• Savour your favourite things
• Do something you feel like doing
• Learn new things
• Connect and share with people
• Help people in need
• Participate in volunteer services

low.title: Well-being is below average
low.description:
Your current physical, psychological, and spiritual well-being is below average, indicating that you may be subject to some physical and mental strain. You may feel tired, less positive and under-nurtured. You may also feel less connected with those around you and your surroundings.

Whenever you feel physically and mentally exhausted, it is important to take care of your own well-being, and find ways to alleviate stress so that you gather strength to tackle life's challenges and live well.

We encourage you to engage in nurturing activities consistently on a daily basis, such as:

• Practise mindfulness
• Exercise regularly
• Connect with nature
• Savour your favourite things
• Do something you feel like doing
• Learn new things
• Meet and share feelings with people around you

If you are currently facing emotional distress, it is recommended to seek professional help for further assessment and advice.

event1.name: Eslite Bookstore | "Sense．To Live" Art Exhibition
event1.description:
Date: 2 March – 30 March
Time: During store opening hours (Eslite Causeway Bay)

Centred on the five senses — sight, sound, smell, taste and touch — the exhibition showcases original works by artists from the Recovery Art Development Programme, alongside a healing sound installation inspired by the song "Coming and Going". You are invited to slow down in the bookstore space and notice your emotions and bodily sensations through colours, lines and sound.

event2.name: Eslite Exclusive | "Returning to the Present through the Five Senses" Talk
event2.description:
Date: 8 March
Time: 2:00 – 3:00 PM

A dialogue led by Clinical Psychologist Yau Yuen Sum from New Life and musician-artist Vicky Fung, exploring how sensory practices can deepen awareness of our surroundings and help us reconnect with the present moment.

event3.name: Eslite Exclusive | Mindful Breathing Experience Workshop
event3.description:
Date: 8 March
Time: 3:00 – 3:30 PM

Led by Clinical Psychologist Yau Yuen Sum, this workshop guides participants through breathing and sound-based practices to reset amidst a busy pace of life and return to the present moment.

event4.name: The Alchemist Café (First Session) | Five-Senses Mindful Eating Workshop
event4.description:
Date: 15 March
Time: 3:00 – 3:30 PM

Starting with a cup of coffee, participants practise slowing down their eating pace and using taste and smell to observe bodily sensations, turning a meal into a quiet moment of dialogue with oneself.

event5.description:

issue1.title: Location still not working after granting permission
issue1.solution1: Ensure your device's GPS function is turned on (usually accessible via the notification drawer)
issue1.solution2: Try closing and reopening the browser or app

issue2.title: Inaccurate location

issue2.solution2: Move to an open outdoor area, avoid tall buildings or indoor environments that may interfere with signals

issue2.solution4: Wait a few minutes for the device to acquire more GPS satellites

issue3.title: Need to reauthorize every time

issue3.solution2: Add this website to your browser's 'Allow List' or 'Trusted Sites'

issue4.solution3: Add the target website to the blocked list

q1.question: Why do I need GPS location?
q1.answer: Some missions require confirmation that you are at a specific location before starting, to ensure you can fully experience the activity content.

q2.question: Will my location information be saved?
q2.answer: We only use location information for verification when you execute missions and do not permanently save your location records. We value your privacy and security.

q3.question: Can I participate using a desktop computer?
q3.answer: We recommend using a GPS-enabled smartphone or tablet for the best experience. Some desktop computers may not support accurate location services.

q4.question: What if it still doesn't work after setup?
q4.answer: Please try restarting your device, or contact our customer service team for assistance.

q1.question: What is the "330 Day City Five Senses Journey"?
q1.answer:
The "330 Day City Five Senses Journey" is an urban interactive experience themed around the five senses (sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch). Participants enter different communities, complete diverse missions, train their awareness, and rediscover familiar yet overlooked details of the city in everyday scenes.

Through exploring street scenery, community sounds, local scents, and human warmth, participants reconnect not only with themselves but also with the city and community, focus on the present, and rediscover a healthy rhythm of mind, body, and spirit.

q2.question: How do I start participating?
q2.answer: Simply visit the designated 330 Day mobile webpage, register an account, and tap "Find Nearby Missions" to start, or browse the mission list to enter a mission. No app download is required.

q3.question: Do I need to register or pay?
q3.answer: All activities are free to participate.

q4.question: Who is the event suitable for?
q4.answer: People of all ages are welcome to join. Some missions involve walking or outdoor activities; please participate according to your physical condition.

q5.question: Can I complete missions more than once?
q5.answer: Each mission counts only once for stamp records, but you are welcome to revisit locations and experience them again.

q1.question: Why use the five senses as the event theme?
q1.answer: The five senses are the foundation of human interaction with the environment. By training awareness of sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch, participants are encouraged to slow down and reconnect with themselves and the city. Multiple psychology and neuroscience studies indicate that focused sensory practices can help reduce stress, improve concentration, and promote emotional stability.

q2.question: What does "awareness" mean?
q2.answer: Awareness means consciously noticing current bodily sensations, emotional changes, and environmental information without rushing to judge or react.

q3.question: What is the "330 Micro-Break"?
q3.answer: The "330 Micro-Break" encourages setting aside a little time each day for body (3), mind (3), and spirit (0), using simple and consistent habits to help relieve stress and stabilize emotions.

q4.question: After completing missions, how can I extend the practice into daily life?
q4.answer: You can integrate five-sense observation into everyday life—for example, mindfully savoring the taste of a meal, noticing layers of city sounds, or feeling different textures, gradually cultivating a habit of awareness.

q1.question: How are missions categorized?
q1.answer: Missions are categorized by the five senses and come in various formats, including observation questions, multiple-choice questions, photo tasks, matching games, or GPS location tasks.

q2.question: Is there a time limit for missions?
q2.answer: There is no time limit for missions; participants can complete them at their own pace.

q3.question: How do I confirm a mission is successfully completed?
q3.answer: A "Mission Completed" message will appear on screen, and a stamp will be automatically recorded.

q4.question: Are there right or wrong answers for missions?
q4.answer: Missions do not have right or wrong answers. Participants simply need to record their feelings in the moment; the goal is to observe and reflect.

q1.question: Why do I need to enable location services?
q1.answer: Each mission requires confirmation that you have arrived at the nearby mission area before it can begin.

q2.question: How do I enable location services?
q2.answer: Please allow "Location Access" in your mobile browser and ensure your phone's GPS is activated.

q3.question: What should I do if I still cannot complete the mission after arriving?
q3.answer: Try refreshing the page, or check whether your location mode is set to "High Accuracy".

q4.question: Will my location be tracked continuously?
q4.answer: The system only reads location data during mission execution and does not store your movements long-term.

q5.question: Can GPS be used at indoor venues?
q5.answer: Some indoor venues may experience location deviations. Please try refreshing the page.

q1.question: Does the website require an app download?
q1.answer: No app download is required; simply participate via your mobile browser.

q2.question: How can I view completed missions?
q2.answer: Go to the "Mission Records" page to view your completed missions.

q3.question: What should I do if the website is not working?
q3.answer: We recommend using the latest version of your browser and maintaining a stable internet connection.

q4.question: Will changing my phone affect my records?
q4.answer: The event has an account login function; simply log in with the same method to retain your records.

q2.question: Is there a limited quantity of gifts?

q3.question: Is there a deadline for redeeming gifts?

q1.question: Can I block passageways or gather during the event?
q1.answer: No. Participants must not block pedestrian passageways, entrances/exits or public spaces, nor gather in ways that cause congestion. Please ensure normal passage for others is not affected.

q2.question: Can I touch, lean on, or use public facilities?
q2.answer: Except under normal usage conditions, participants must not touch, climb, or lean on public facilities. Event missions do not involve any facility operation; please comply with venue rules.

q3.question: What should I be aware of when doing photography or video tasks?
q3.answer: Please avoid obstructing others or disrupting public order, and do not perform dangerous actions. Respect others' privacy when photographing and do not photograph individuals without their consent.

q4.question: Do minors need to be accompanied when participating?
q4.answer: Participants under 12 years of age are recommended to be accompanied by a parent or guardian, who should assess safety conditions on site.
